properties.name: Mount Rainier
properties.subtitle: Pierce County, Washington, United States
properties.claim: On 24 June 1947 the pilot Kenneth Arnold reported nine crescent objects weaving between Rainier and Mount Adams at an estimated 1,700 mph — the sighting that gave the world the phrase 'flying saucer' and opened the modern era.
properties.context: Arnold's report is the origin point of the entire phenomenon as a public category, and the term itself came from a reporter's compression of his description of how the objects moved, not their shape. Proposed explanations include a formation of pelicans, lenticular cloud and mirage effects over the Cascades; Arnold rejected all of them and never recanted. Rainier is an active, heavily glaciated stratovolcano and the most dangerous volcano in the contiguous US by lahar risk.
properties.summary: On June 24, 1947, private pilot Kenneth Arnold saw what he described as a string of nine shiny unidentified flying objects flying past Mount Rainier at speeds that he estimated to be at least 1,200 miles per hour (1,900 km/h).
